messages:
nora-cs: Customer NebulaPay reports SSO broken right after their IdP cert rotation. Users hit 403 on our /sso/acs endpoint. Raising to eng, attaching snippets below.

aj-eng: Thanks — can you paste the failing request/response and the metadata fetch? quick repro steps please.

nora-cs: Repro steps from the customer: 1) Click SP login -> 2) Redirect to IdP -> 3) After auth redirect back to our ACS we get 403.

nora-cs: Curl of the ACS callback (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST 'https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/acs'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
  --data 'SAMLResponse=...&RelayState=...'
```
Response headers we received: 302 -> then 403 on POST:
```
HTTP/2 302
location: /sso/acs/handle
content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-16
content-encoding: gzip
server: cdn-edge-12

HTTP/2 403
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
```

aj-eng: Hmm two odd things: content-type mentions UTF-16 on the idp side, and CDN rewrote the path to add/remove trailing slash. Can you paste the IdP metadata URL and what our metadata fetcher logged?

maria-sre: I pulled our metadata fetch logs — the downloader fetched their metadata but logged "skipping KeyDescriptor: xml parse error (encoding mismatch)". The raw body started with a BOM followed by UTF-16 declaration, and our fetcher currently trusts Content-Type header and tries to decode as UTF-8. That can cause the SignedKey to be ignored.

maria-sre: Log excerpt:
```
[2026-09-02T14:03:12Z] fetcher: GET https://idp.nebula.example/metadata -> 200 (gzip)
[2026-09-02T14:03:12Z] fetcher: content-type 'text/xml; charset=utf-16'
[2026-09-02T14:03:12Z] xml: parse warning: detected BOM, using UTF-16LE
[2026-09-02T14:03:12Z] metadata: KeyDescriptor (signing) not found after parse -> metadata considered unsigned
```

devon-platform: Also noticed our recent metadata cache change (rolled two deploys ago) started honoring Content-Type strictly and stopped doing a normalization pass that fixed trailing-slash differences in entityIDs. The IdP's EntityID is "https://nebula.example/idp" while the metadata they uploaded and the redirect references "https://nebula.example/idp/" (trailing slash). Our lookup failed because we compare normalized entityIDs now only after decode step which didn't run due to parse error. Chain reaction.

aj-eng: So root cause hypothesis: IdP served metadata with UTF-16 BOM which our fetcher mishandled -> parser failed to surface signing KeyDescriptor -> metadata treated as unsigned -> we fell back to stricter entityID matching which also failed because of trailing-slash mismatch -> final result 403.

nora-cs: Customer asks for workaround while we fix: is there a quick config they can change on their IdP or on our side? They can re-upload metadata.

maria-sre: Short-term workaround: Request Nebula to re-publish metadata as UTF-8 (or remove BOM). Alternatively we can clear metadata cache and force a re-fetch with an override that forces correct charset detection. I can run a one-off re-fetch with lenient encoding heuristics.

aj-eng: Agreed. Also for safety add an alias mapping: accept both entityID with and without trailing slash for a short window. We'll patch the normalization fallback within the metadata service.

nora-cs: Can you run the re-fetch now? Customer on call waiting.

maria-sre: Doing it now — hitting our /internal/metadata/refetch endpoint for idp entity id "https://nebula.example/idp":
```
POST /internal/metadata/refetch HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-api.redwood
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{"entity_id":"https://nebula.example/idp","force_charset_detection":true}
```

maria-sre: refetch result: 200 OK, parser used UTF-16LE, SignedKey extracted. Also added temporary alias for entityID with trailing slash.

maria-sre: After re-fetch our logs:
```
[2026-09-02T14:08:23Z] metadata: Signed Key found (KeyDescriptor use accepted)
[2026-09-02T14:08:24Z] routing: entity_id normalized-> matched alias https://nebula.example/idp/
[2026-09-02T14:08:24Z] acs: successful assertion validated -> user session created
```

devon-platform: I've kicked a rollback on the metadata-fix change to restore the previous normalization pass while we push a safer parser fix. deploy-bot says: rollback in progress.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback started for service=metadata-fetcher tag=2026.08.30. Confirmed rollback successful on 3 nodes.

aj-eng: Next steps: 1) Add robust charset detection to metadata fetcher (detect BOM and honor xml declaration regardless of Content-Type). 2) Add tolerant entityID matching (strip or add trailing slash) as a config option for 30d. 3) Add automated validation for re-homed cert rotations. I'll open an RFC and assign follow-ups.

nora-cs: Customer confirmed login succeeded after you re-fetched and we cleared their sessions. They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

aj-eng: I'll post ETA in #eng-releases once RFC is merged; aim to have parser fix and entityID-tolerance out in next patch (48–72 hours).

maria-sre: For now I've left the alias mapping and forced refetch in place. Monitoring for 2h. If no regressions, we'll keep alias for 7 days.

nora-cs: Thanks team — marking this resolved for the customer. :thumbsup:

aj-eng: reassigning to devon-platform for follow-up tasks and RFC.

devon-platform: Got it — creating follow-up tickets and linking to this thread.

nora-cs: Closing on our side once customer confirms no more errors in 1 hour.
